newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Output halved at Nigeria's Port-Harcourt refinery.
newsitem.headline: Output halved at Nigeria's Port-Harcourt refinery.

text.p: Production output in Nigeria's southeastern Port-Harcourt refinery has dropped to 50 percent capacity due to a damage to the operation control unit, the semi-official Daily Times reported on Monday.

It quoted an official of state oil company NNPC as saying the development could worsen the on-going fuel shortages that hit the commercial capital Lagos last week and had spread to some neighbouring towns.
NNPC officials were not immediately available for comments.

"A damage to the operation control unit of the refinery has reduced production to 50 percent from its total capacity," the paper quoted the official as saying, adding that he did not state reason for the damage.
On Saturday, NNPC said in a statement the nation's four refineries were operating normally despite the fuel crisis, the fifth this year.

It was silent on the operating capacity of the Port-Harcourt refinery, but said the second refinery in the same city and those of midwestern Warri and northern Kaduna had each been operating steadily in the past three weeks at 60 and 70 percent, respectively.
The refineries have a combined theoretical capacity of 445,000 barrels per day but poor management has made production reduce to well below that.
As a result, Nigeria has had to frequently import fuel to stem shortages, a common phenomenon in Africa's largest producer of crude oil.
Motorists said vehicles still jammed pump stations on Monday in search of petrol as the fuel shortages continued to bite hard.
Thousands of commuters were stranded along major roads while commercial buses and taxis maintained the two-fold fare hike they resorted to since last week when the fuel crunch began.
"We have not lifted supplies at depots since Friday and it is unclear how this crisis will be resolved," Amos Jimoh, one tanker driver, told Reuters.

Industry sources, citing a dispute between Petroleum Tanker Drivers' Association and the National Asociation of Road Transport Owners, last week warned of disruption in fuel distribution in the run-up to the Easter holiday this weekend.
There has been no comment from both unions.
